mainText:
The final election result is deadlocked, with Christopher Luxon admitting lengthy coalition talks lie ahead and the Opportunity Party holding the balance of power.

New Zealand.

The twenty twenty six election has produced a hung Parliament. Christopher Luxon needs Opportunity, New Zealand First and ACT together to govern, and Chris Hipkins has no path to power without them. Opportunity's Qiulae Wong says voters sent a message for change, not compromise. David Seymour has pitched himself for Finance Minister. Candidates have until Wednesday the second of December to apply for recounts in the tightest seats. National's Mike Butterick lost Wairarapa to Labour's Kieran McAnulty by fewer than one hundred votes. Economist Shamubeel Eaqub says the economy will be largely unaffected regardless of outcome, since there is little real difference between National and Labour on economic policy.

The Black Caps are struggling on day two of the second test against India at Hagley Oval in Christchurch. India's bowlers have put the home side on the back foot with a wicket blitz after a promising start.

One person is critically injured after a car and truck crash closed Morrinsville-Tahuna Road in Waikato, reported just after six thirty yesterday morning.

A mechanical failure at Wellington's Western wastewater plant means partially treated wastewater is reaching Cook Strait near Karori Stream, according to Tiaki Wai.

In the Bay of Plenty, a live adult male cane toad has been captured at Tauriko after being spotted by firefighters who reported it to biosecurity authorities. The poisonous invasive species is not established in New Zealand, and officials are checking the area for others.

Fire and Emergency has brought in fire restrictions in inland Otago, with dry, windy conditions rapidly increasing risk as a strong El Niño pattern develops. Separately, MetService has issued severe weather watches with temperatures forecast to reach twenty eight degrees this weekend, with hot, dry winds adding to fire danger nationally.

World.

Ukraine's president Volodymyr Zelensky has told the BBC that Donald Trump's friendship with Vladimir Putin is strange, saying the United States is not pushing Russia hard enough to end the war. Kyiv is bracing for another winter of fighting with no sign either side will back down.

Poundland has collapsed into administration, putting eleven thousand jobs at risk after its American owners, Gordon Brothers, failed to find a buyer. The chain's closure timeline is still being worked out.

Severe Thanksgiving storms have brought flooding and fallen trees to both coasts of the United States, with hundreds of thousands of properties left without power.

A capsized tanker carrying seven thousand tonnes of diesel is being towed away from Ibiza. Spanish authorities say the vessel's fuel tanks remain intact, easing immediate spill fears.

Technology.

Nvidia's value has climbed by almost one trillion dollars and tech stocks have rallied since Jensen Huang's return as chief executive, lifting the Nasdaq by six and a half per cent. The United States attorney general has still dodged questions about an investigation into Huang, and lawmakers are demanding answers about Donald Trump's role in his reinstatement. The US is separately preparing to blacklist the Asian firm Megaspeed, accused of funnelling Nvidia chips to China after a former executive's affair with Huang became public. BBC analysts say fears of an AI bubble that existed before Huang's exit have not gone away.

Sport.

Rugby. Italy beat Fiji twenty three to twenty one in London, their eleventh placing in the Nations Championship, ending a losing streak after surviving late Fijian pressure. Ireland beat Australia thirty eight to fourteen in the same competition's autumn finale, finishing fifth. The All Blacks play England at Twickenham this weekend under new captain Jordie Barrett, with six changes made after last week's loss, which coach Dave Rennie says still hurts.

Cricket. The Black Caps are under pressure against India on day two at Hagley Oval, losing wickets steadily after a promising start. Full detail to follow as play continues.

Boxing. Joseph Parker fights Daniel Dubois for the WBO heavyweight title in his comeback bout, his first since a loss last October and his first world title shot since twenty seventeen. Pundits say ring rust could count against him.

Basketball. The Tall Blacks beat Jordan one hundred and three to sixty four, as Jordan Ngatai marked his one hundredth game for the side.

League. Tickets for the historic State of Origin match at Eden Park have almost sold out, with remaining seats priced between three hundred and four hundred and fifty two dollars.

Formula One. Liam Lawson says he is less experienced than he appears, reflecting on a difficult season as the year winds down.

Coming up. The All Blacks play England at Twickenham this weekend. The Black Caps continue day two against India in Christchurch today. Joseph Parker fights Daniel Dubois for the WBO heavyweight title. Coalition talks between National, ACT, New Zealand First and Opportunity continue this week, with no government expected before Christmas.

End of flash.
